annotation.evidence_span: Servers MAY serve HTTP/3 on any UDP port
annotation.interpretation_a: A server could choose to serve HTTP/3 on a different UDP port for each connection, requiring clients to dynamically discover the port.
annotation.interpretation_b: A server could consistently serve HTTP/3 on a single, well-known UDP port, simplifying client configuration.
annotation.justification: The use of "MAY" combined with "any UDP port" allows for two reasonable interpretations regarding port assignment. A server could use a fixed port or a dynamically assigned port, and the clause does not constrain this choice. This impacts client implementation because a client needs to be able to handle both scenarios.
annotation.missing_information: The clause does not specify whether servers are expected to use a consistent port for HTTP/3 or if dynamic port assignment is allowed. This affects client implementation as it determines whether clients need to support dynamic port discovery.
